title: The Brew Shop - Weekly Email Update
contentHtml:
Hey Brew Shop Fam!
Here's an update of what's happening this week - from new beer drops, wine reviews, our current tap list, to upcoming tastings, and more. 

SHOP THIS WEEK’S NEWSLETTER HERE SHOP OUR ENTIRE STOCK OF BEER, WINE & HOMEBREW HERE

Join us this Friday from 5-7 PM as we welcome Great Lakes for our free tasting! Scroll down to the bottom of our newsletter to see the full line-up for next month!

TONIGHT! Join us for an evening filled with books and wine with special guest The Wandering Shelf! We’re creating a spin off from the beloved Scholastic Book Fair we attended as kids, with plenty of books on hand to go with our free wine tasting.

It’s our Wine Club pickup tasting and everyone is invited! Sip and browse a fun curation of books and bookish goods for adults (& a few special goodies for your kids!) Tessa, owner of The Wandering Shelf, will be here to chat all things books with you while you check out what our Wine Club is all about with a free tasting of this month’s Wine Club wines. Wine Club Members get special discounts on books, and book purchasers get a chance at a free membership to our Wine Club! Come by anytime from 5-8pm TONIGHT, 9/24, and check it out!

Biohof Pratsch Gruner Veltliner: This bottle reminds us exactly why Gruner Veltliner is so under-the-radar delicious with pear, white pepper, lemon zest and salty minerality. The perfect bottle to reach for when you want something food-friendly and endlessly drinkable. Organic.

Kermit Lynch Cotes-du-Rhone Villages Rouge: Sometimes we discover a wine when we're out of town and know that we must get it to our shelves immediately. Having absolutely crushed a bottle of this with friends in Michigan, I can say firsthand it's not just my palate that was smitten with this Rhone beauty. From renowned importer Kermit Lynch comes a wine that's as gorgeous in taste as it is in color. Juicy dark fruit, black pepper and herbs, plush tannins, and a balanced acidity make for an elegant and crowd pleasing bottle. Organic.

Chateau Trebiac Bordeaux Rouge: A classic left-bank Bordeaux blend that toes the line perfectly between jammy fruit and dusty tannins. Aged three months in French oak, Chateau Trebiac delivers with ripe red berries, dark chocolate and savory notes reminiscent of cigar box adding a touch of refinement. Sustainable.

Lapis Luna Cabernet Sauvignon: High five for a Wine Enthusiast Best Buy! Lapis Luna is your next crusher Cabernet Sauvignon. Full-bodied and velvety with loads of ripe fruit, baking spices and a touch of vanilla.

Lurton Araucano Humo Blanco Carmenere: François Lurton — part of the legendary Bordeaux winemaking dynasty — fell so in love with the Chilean terroir that in 2000 he planted vines near the historic town of Lolol in Colchagua Valley. Grown on ocean-influenced clay and volcanic sedimentary soils, Humo Blanco (aka "white smoke") warms you from within with plum, blackberry, clove, peppery spice, and that classic Carmenere herbal edge that makes it unlike anything else in the wine world. Organic.

It’s officially fall! You know what that means? It means I can write about red wine and drink a pumpkin beer without feeling distressing seasonal guilt. Ladies and gentlemen of the red wine committee, we are SO back. Allow me to introduce this beautiful new Spanish red, your perfect intro bottle for fall, Bodegas Ochoa Labrit Garnacha. Labrit is a particularly fun bottle for anyone who saw "Spanish red" and immediately thought big Rioja or Tempranillo. While I'm not going to throw a heavy-ass red in your face the moment September 22nd crosses our calendars (Like, obviously I'll wait for October), I am going to hit you with a gorgeous Garnacha and call it a compromise.

Hailing from northern Spain, Bodegas Ochoa has been making wine in Navarra for generations, and the estate has a long history of championing native Spanish grapes while embracing more modern winemaking. For this particular wine, grapes were sourced from organic vineyards with 200 recovered biotypes of ancestral Garnacha. Expect ripe red berries, raspberry and cherry, with some subtle floral and spicy notes hanging around in the background. Half the wine spends 6 months in French Oak, and the other half remains in concrete, making it medium-bodied with soft tannins and enough freshness to keep things lively. This is dangerously easy to drink, and so perfect for the weather we're currently having. Basically, it has the confidence of a big red wine without needing to yell about it (like I said, compromise).

Crack this open alongside roasted chicken, root vegetables, pizza, or honestly whatever cozy fall meal you’ve got going on. If you're like me, you're having a glass of this while reading a book, cozied up on your couch. While also watching the rain. And also snuggling with your dog. Look at that, I've just found my weekend plans. It's still approachable enough for a weeknight, interesting enough to actually talk about, and exactly the kind of bottle to jumpstart fall. Welcome back, red wine season. I missed you.

This week’s writeup is brought to you by Aidan

Thanks for your business! See you soon, Beth, Julie & Aidan and the entire Brew Crew
